item.title: Comprehensive Guide to RTI Proactive Disclosure and Internal Audit Functions in Sikkim
item.description:
Comprehensive Guide to RTI Proactive Disclosure and Internal Audit Functions in Sikkim

Transparency and accountability are the bedrock of effective financial management in government. Under Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, public authorities are mandated to proactively disclose key information regarding their organization, functions, duties, and operational procedures. This proactive disclosure minimizes the necessity for individual citizens to file formal requests while fostering public trust.

This article details the institutional framework, RTI proactive disclosures, and core objectives of both the Sikkim Local Fund Audit (SLFA) and the Internal Audit (IA) Division under the Finance Department, Government of Sikkim.

item.title: Resolving Institutional Deadlocks: Drafting Official Audit Noting for XVI Finance Commission Grants
item.description:
Introduction

When state austerity directives, strict budget restrictions during a Vote on Account period, and rigid biometric attendance mandates collide, essential public administration processes can ground to a complete halt.

This case study demonstrates the iterative drafting of an official office noting for the Directorate of Local Fund Audit (DLFA)[cite: 1]. The objective is to present a crisp, highly structured executive note seeking administrative waivers, emergency fund releases, or explicit deferment directives from higher authorities to safeguard central grants under the 16th Finance Commission (XVI FC)[cite: 1].

item.title: Standardizing Transparency: A Complete Guide to Proactive Disclosure Under Section 4 of the RTI Act
item.description:
Transparency in public administration forms the cornerstone of accountability and public trust. Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, mandates every public authority to proactively disclose detailed organizational data. This statutory requirement ensures that citizens have seamless access to routine administrative records without having to repeatedly file individual RTI requests.

To streamline compliance across municipal, state, and central institutions, adopting a structured, standardized, and fillable template is essential. Below is a comprehensive, end-to-end framework that public authorities can implement to fulfill all statutory requirements under Section 4(1)(b).
